newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo's losses.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo's losses.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower, extending Wednesday's losses as buyers remained sidelined on expectations of cheaper prices, dealers said.

"There were only scattered demand in the market. Buyers are just not willing to commit heavily," a dealer at a trading firm said, adding that prices could fall further in the near-term due to uncertainty in Tokyo and cheaper Indonesian rubber.
Some Asian enquiries were seen for sheet and SMR 20 but only selective business was done through hand-to-mouth basis.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 283 cents a kg for May, SMR CV at 351, SMR L at 330, SMR 5 at 290, SMR 10 at 285 and drum latex FOB at 235/236.
At the close, May RSS Ones eased half a cent to 296 cents ($1.19) a kg and May SMR 20 buyer was down two to 281.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 227.52 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on April 2 from 228.01 on April 1.
